title: Integrated GPU Fleet + Cloud Accounts + IaC + CI/CD Playbook
author: Marcus Li
content:
Summary

This playbook consolidates operational guidance for: GPU fleet capacity planning, cloud account and networking setup, Terraform/IaC module patterns, CI/CD build pipelines for infra changes, and runbooks used by on-call and capacity teams. It is intended for infra engineers, SREs, and platform owners responsible for maintaining predictable GPU-backed inference capacity across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Scope

- Applies to public cloud GPU fleets (AWS and GCP) and related cloud accounts used for shared inference capacity.
- Covers IaC patterns (Terraform modules), CI/CD gating, and runbook procedures for capacity incidents and planned capacity changes.
- Excludes on-prem appliance packaging details (see eng-private-deployments/reference-architectures).

Owner and contacts

- Document owner: Marcus Li (Platform Infrastructure)
- Primary on-call: infra-sre rotation (pager: #infra-oncall)
- Tier 2 escalation: Diego Hernandez (GPU Fleet), Priya Rao (Networking)

Definitions

- GPU pool: a logical group of instances (or nodepools) with compatible GPU type and networking profile used for serving.
- Allocation group: customer-facing capacity reservation mapped to one or more GPU pools.
- Warm/Cold pool: warm = pre-provisioned nodes ready to accept workloads within target spin-up time; cold = capacity available via scale-up but with longer provisioning window.

Architecture overview

High-level requirements:
- Multi-region pools per production region to meet latency SLOs.
- Separate cloud accounts for infrastructure, shared GPU fleet, and customer-dedicated capacity (for billing/segmentation and least-privilege).
- IaC-managed networking (VPCs, subnets, routing, NSGs) with explicit peering and service endpoints for the control plane.

Design principles:
- Immutable infrastructure via Terraform modules; small, composable modules per domain (compute, networking, iam, monitoring).
- GitOps-driven CI/CD with policy checks and automated plan approvals for low-risk changes.
- Tagging and metadata on all resources for cost and ownership tracking.

Capacity planning and targets

Operational SLOs (examples):
- Average GPU utilization target: 55% (goal to maximize utilization while keeping headroom for burst).
- Scale-up latency SLO: 95th percentile < 5 minutes for warm pool scaling; cold pool < 15 minutes.
- Headroom target: maintain 10% spare capacity across regions for emergency scaling.

Capacity thresholds and alerts:
- Warning: regional GPU utilization > 70% sustained for 10m -> create ticket and notify capacity team.
- Critical: regional GPU utilization > 85% sustained for 5m OR free GPU slot count < configured emergency threshold -> page on-call and begin emergency scale flow.

Capacity table (example)

| Region | Pool Type | Baseline Nodes | Warm Nodes | Emergency Threshold | Owner |
|--------|-----------|----------------|------------|---------------------|-------|
| us-west-2 | A100-pool | 40 | 20 | 8 | infra-west |
| eu-west-1 | H100-pool | 32 | 16 | 6 | infra-eu |

Cloud accounts and networking

Account strategy:
1. infra-control: centralized account for global infra tooling (monitoring, CI runners, state storage).
2. gpu-shared: shared GPU fleet accounts per cloud and primary region.
3. customer-dedicated: per-enterprise account(s) for dedicated capacity and isolation.

Networking guidelines:
- VPC per account with standardized subnet layout (public management subnets, private compute subnets, restricted management access via bastion).
- Use Transit Gateway (AWS) / Shared VPC (GCP) for controlled connectivity between control plane and GPU pools.
- Network ACLs and security groups: default deny inbound to compute subnets; control-plane control-plane egress only to monitoring endpoints.

IAM and least privilege:
- Role-based access in each account; cross-account roles for automation with short-lived credentials.
- Terraform state is secured in an encryption-enabled, access-restricted S3/GCS bucket; state locker uses DynamoDB/CloudLock.

Terraform / IaC modules and patterns

Module boundaries (recommended):
- module/networking: VPC, subnets, route tables, transit attachment.
- module/compute: node pools, instance templates, auto-repair policies.
- module/gpu-profile: AMI/container image, drivers, MIG/partitioning, nvlink topology when applicable.
- module/iam: roles, instance profiles, service accounts, policies for least privilege.
- module/monitoring: log sinks, metric exports, alerting endpoints.

Best practices:
- All modules must include examples/usage, variables with defaults, outputs for integration points, and a CHANGELOG.md.
- Keep modules small and composable; prefer composition over monolith modules.
- Use numeric versions and release tags for published modules; require module source pinning in environments.
- Enforce pre-commit linting: tflint, terraform fmt, checkov for policy violations.

Example module configuration snippet (Terraform HCL - shown as text):

terraform {
  required_providers {
    aws = { source = "hashicorp/aws" version = "~> 4.0" }
  }
  backend "s3" {
    bucket = "redwood-terraform-state"
    key    = "gpu-shared/us-west-2/compute.tfstate"
    region = "us-west-2"
    encrypt = true
  }
}

module "compute_gpu_pool" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules.git//compute?ref=v1.3.0"
  name   = "a100-pool-usw2"
  instance_type = "p4d.24xlarge"
  desired_capacity = 40
  warm_capacity = 20
  tags = { team = "infra-west" service = "gpu-serving" }
}

CI/CD and build patterns

Pipeline stages (recommended):
1. terraform fmt + validate (pre-commit)
2. static analysis: tflint, checkov, tfsec
3. terraform plan (with environment variables for account/region) -> produce plan artifact
4. policy unit tests (rego/opa) and cost estimate check
5. Manual approval gate for high-risk changes (e.g., > 10% capacity change, networking changes)
6. terraform apply in gated runner with short-lived credentials

Branching and approvals:
- Use protected branches for environment promotion: feature -> staging -> prod. Promotion requires passing checks and at least one approver from owning team.
- Auto-merge allowed for low-risk changes (tagged docs-only or small tags) with 2 green CI checks.

Runner and credentials:
- CI runners run in infra-control account with OIDC-based short-lived credentials and limited cross-account assume-role permissions.
- Each pipeline run logs plan output to a centralized artifact store for audit.

Runbooks and operational playbooks

Common incidents and play flows:

1) Incident: Regional capacity critical (utilization > 85%)
- Step 1: On-call acknowledges page and triages region (check scaling history, pending nodes, control plane logs).
- Step 2: If warm pool exhausted, trigger emergency scale (manual increase of desired_capacity by pre-approved emergency delta).
- Step 3: If scale fails, fall back to routing policy: divert new requests to secondary region or lower-cost model variant (follow routing runbook).
- Step 4: After mitigation, create a post-incident ticket, update capacity forecast if trend persists.

2) Incident: Failed Terraform apply in prod pipeline
- Step 1: Do not retry apply. Revoke the pipeline runner token and collect plan artifact.
- Step 2: Roll back using last known good state for the affected module. If state drift is suspected, run terraform plan with -refresh and reconcile.
- Step 3: Pager to module owner and open a JIRA for root-cause analysis.

3) Routine: Planned capacity expansion
- Step 1: Create capacity request in capacity-tracker with expected date, justification, and cost estimate.
- Step 2: Run a dry-run (terraform plan in staging account) and execute canary increase in a single availability zone. Monitor metrics for 24 hours.
- Step 3: If metrics within thresholds, roll out to remaining AZs/regions using automated pipeline with staged increases (10% -> 50% -> 100%).

Operational checklists

Pre-deploy checklist for compute changes:
- [ ] Module version pinned and changelog reviewed
- [ ] Plan output reviewed by owner and infra-sre
- [ ] Backup of related state and snapshot of critical volumes
- [ ] Monitoring dashboards have expected widgets updated

Post-deploy verification:
- Verify desired_capacity matches expected
- Confirm node health and driver installation across the pool
- Confirm alerting thresholds are firing at expected levels and billing tags are applied

Auditing and cost control

- Tag enforcement policy: cost center, owner, project, environment — enforced via pre-apply policy checks.
- Daily cost report ingested into finance toolkit; unexpected spend triggers review with finance and platform.

Change management and governance

- Large networking changes or multi-account IAM changes require RFC and approval from Security and Platform leads.
- Maintain a quarterly capacity review with product, sales (to map committed reserved capacity), and finance.

Appendix: quick troubleshooting commands

- List GPU nodes (k8s): kubectl get nodes -l gpu=true -o wide
- Check node GPU utilization (ssh to node): nvidia-smi dmon -s u
- Terraform plan for environment: TF_VAR_region=us-west-2 terraform plan -var-file=env/prod.tfvars

Related documents

- infra-iac-and-gpu-fleet-guide-2026 (module reference and driver packaging)

Notes and next steps
